messages:
alex: Heads-up: after the batching-heuristic tweak in #PR-482 we saw a 12-18% p99 regression on long-context 32k runs in the perf CI. I ran an nsys capture and perfetto; looks like kernel selection is sometimes happening inside a big batch assembly window which pushes the critical path. Posting snippets and a few questions.

alex: nsys command I used: `nsys profile -o out/serving_trace -t cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range full --sample=none python -m perf.run_long_context`

alex: on the nvtx timeline I see: 
```
NVTX: serving.request.start (req_id=0x7f3)
  NVTX: batching.assembly.start
    NVTX: batch.coalesce
    NVTX: serving.kernsel.choose_kernel
    NVTX: cuda.kernel.launch conv_fused
  NVTX: batching.assembly.end
NVTX: serving.kvcache.lookup (HIT)
NVTX: serving.request.end
```

alex: two quick questions: should kernel selection be inside the batching span? and should we emit separate kvcache.hit / kvcache.miss ranges per request or keep them aggregated by worker?

maya: hmm interesting. i think kernel selection inside batching makes it hard to attribute latency to kernel chooser vs batch scheduling. i'd prefer separate span for kernel.choice so we can filter by req_id.

ben: agree. separate spans per request make traces larger but they’re invaluable for root-cause. maybe we cap them to only be emitted for sampled traces (1%) and lightweight counters otherwise. :thumbsup:

liz: +1. also we should standardize naming so downstream analysis can query easily. proposal: `srv.req.<req_component>.<op>` e.g. `srv.req.kernsel.choose` `srv.req.batching.assemble` `srv.req.kv.hit` `srv.req.kv.miss`

alex: naming looks good. ps: observed some weirdness: a few kernels are chosen *after* KV cache lookup in the timeline which doesn't make sense — might be that NVTX ranges got ordered by wall-clock vs cuda-stream. we should ensure we push NVTX ranges on the correct stream.

ben: important point. NVTX pushed on host thread doesn't guarantee ordering relative to GPU work if kernels are launched on different streams. we should use `nvtxRangePushEx` with `nvtxDomain` tied to stream if possible, and also annotate stream id in the range name: `srv.stream=3,kernsel.choose`.

maya: for implementation: 1) add a per-request span for kernsel outside batching assembly; 2) keep batching.assembly as a higher-level span; 3) emit kvcache.{hit,miss} as spans but only when `TRACE_SAMPLING_RATE>0` or when debug flag set.

alex: sketch of code diffs: 
```
// before: inside batch_assemble()
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("batching.assembly");
  // do coalesce
  NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("serving.kernsel.choose_kernel");
  choose_kernel(...);
  NVTX_RANGE_POP();
NVTX_RANGE_POP();

// after: move kernsel out
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("batching.assembly");
  // coalesce
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
// per-request
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH_FMT("srv.req.kernsel.choose req=%s stream=%d", req_id, stream_id);
choose_kernel(...);
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```

liz: for sampling, we should add a sampling header on the request object (bool trace_sampled) and avoid the expensive string formatting when false. also avoid pushing thousands of tiny NVTX ranges for small ops — group micro-ops into `srv.req.kernsel.detail` when trace_sampled=false.

infra-bot: perf-ci run 4822 finished: p99 increased by 14.2% on bench/long_context_32k — investigating.

alex: fyi attached perfetto link (internal) and a small screenshot. the perfetto view shows kernsel compute block interleaving with batch serialization.

maya: another practical: we must ensure kvcache spans are emitted on the same host thread that issues the cuda kernel (or at least include coro id) so we can correlate. questionable to tie them to worker-global counters only.

ben: agreed. and add a field `span_id` unique per request + per-op to help correlating traces across nsight/nvtx/perfetto. e.g. `srv.span=0x1a2b` in the nvtx name/meta.

alex: acceptance criteria for the change: 
- NVTX per-request kernsel spans emitted for sampled traces
- Batching.assembly remains as a macro span but excludes kernsel duration
- KV cache emits hit/miss spans for sampled traces and emits counters for unsampled
- Naming follows `srv.req.<component>.<op>` with optional `span` and `stream` tags in the string
- No more than +2% regression on p99 in perf CI for long context after change

liz: sounds reasonable. can we run a small AB test in CI: current master vs branch with nvtx-change at 10% sampling to validate perf impact?

alex: yes i'll land an experimental build with `NVTX_SAMPLING=0.1` and run perf CI subset (long_context_32k, short_8k) and post results.

maya: small nit: avoid `.` as separator in span names for numeric fields; prefer comma-separated key=val in metadata part: `srv.req.kernsel.choose span=0x1a2b,stream=3` so queries can split by dot for component path.

ben: good call. also add a backend mapping table in docs (devex) so `srv.req.kernsel` maps to codepath `runtime/kernsel.*` for quick triage.

alex: ok i'll draft the PR with code sketch + tests for NVTX ordering (push on the same thread/stream) and add perf CI jobs. tagging @maya @ben @liz for review.

liz: thx. if perf looks stable we should enable sampled spans globally at 0.5% in staging to get more signal.

infra-bot: created perf run 4823 for branch `nvtx-kernsel-sampling` — will post results in ~45m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
